;Armed conflict and attacks
*Thirty-two people are killed when [[Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant|Islamic State members]] started a prison riot and a fire in a prison located in [[Vahdat]], [[Tajikistan]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-asia-48332969 (BBC News)] [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2019/05/isil-inmates-spark-deadly-riot-tajik-prison-190520060419825.html (Al Jazeera)] [https://www.rt.com/news/459783-isis-riot-tajikistan-prison/ (RT)]
;Arts and culture
*[[Whole Foods Market]] announces it will eliminate disposable [[Drinking straw|plastic straws]] in July from its stores in the [[United States]], [[Canada]] and the [[United Kingdom]]. [https://www.usatoday.com/story/money/2019/05/20/whole-foods-drop-plastic-straws-us-stores-july/3739491002/ (''USA Today'')]

;Business and finance
*[[Ascena Retail Group]] announces it will close all 650 Dressbarn stores by the end of the year. [https://www.usatoday.com/story/money/2019/05/20/dressbarn-closing-all-stores/3747205002/ (''USA Today'')]

;Disasters and accidents
*Two people are killed, the pilot and the passenger, when a [[Floatplane|floatplane]] crashes into [[Metlakatla, Alaska|Metlakatla]] harbor near [[Ketchikan, Alaska|Ketchikan]], [[Alaska]]. The pilot and passenger were the only people on board. [https://www.cbsnews.com/news/alaska-small-plane-crash-kills-2-a-week-after-a-deadly-mid-air-collision-involving-the-same-carrier/ (CBS News)] [https://www.nbcnews.com/news/us-news/two-dead-after-float-plane-crashes-alaska-n1008131 (NBC News)]

;International relations 
*[[North Korea–South Korea relations]], [[Droughts in Korea]]
**[[South Korea]] vows to send humanitarian aid to [[North Korea]] through international organizations as it suffers droughts. [http://www.startribune.com/south-korea-vows-to-send-aid-to-north-quickly-may-send-food/510152332/ (''Star Tribune'')] [https://www.nytimes.com/aponline/2019/05/20/world/asia/ap-as-koreas-diplomacy-.html (''The New York Times'')]

*[[Iran–Saudi Arabia relations]], [[Iran–United States relations]]
**[[Iran]]ian [[List of Ministers of Foreign Affairs of Iran|Minister of Foreign Affairs]] [[Mohammad Javad Zarif]] states that the "genocidal taunts" of [[President of the United States|U.S. President]] [[Donald Trump]] "won't end Iran", in response to President Trump's comments that if Iran attacked U.S. interests, "that will be the official end of Iran." He also blasted [[Saudi Arabia]]n [[Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Saudi Arabia)|Minister of Foreign Affairs]] [[Adel al-Jubeir]] for his previous May 19 remarks regarding Iran. [https://www.brecorder.com/2019/05/20/498069/tehran-says-trumps-genocidal-taunts-wont-end-iran/ (''Brecorder'')]
*[[Russia–United States relations]]
**U.S. [[Lockheed Martin F-22 Raptor|F-22 stealth jets]] intercept four [[Russia|Russian]] [[Tupolev Tu-95]] strategic bombers and two Russian [[Sukhoi Su-35|Su-35]] jets entering the Alaskan Air Defense Identification Zone off the coast of [[Alaska]]. The Russian jets and bombers did not enter the [[United States|U.S.]] nor [[Canada|Canadian]] airspace according to the [[North American Aerospace Defense Command]]. [https://www.cbsnews.com/news/russian-jets-bombers-intercepted-by-us-near-alaska-coast-norad-says-today-2019-05-21/ (CBS News)] [https://www.cnn.com/2019/05/21/politics/russian-bombers-alaska-intercept/index.html (CNN)]

;Law and crime
*The [[Sweden|Swedish]] [[Swedish Prosecution Authority|prosecutor]] files an arrest warrant against [[WikiLeaks]] founder [[Julian Assange]] over a rape allegation. Assange is serving a 50-week prison sentence in the [[United Kingdom]] for skipping bail. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-wikileaks-assange-sweden-detention/swedish-prosecutor-files-request-for-assanges-arrest-over-rape-allegation-idUSKCN1SQ0ID (Reuters)]
*The [[Supreme Court of the United States|U.S. Supreme Court]] in ''Herrera v. Wyoming'' rules in favor of a [[Native Americans in the United States|Native American]] [[Elk|elk]] hunter from [[Montana]] who was convicted for hunting {{nowrap|off-season}} in [[Bighorn National Forest]], deciding that the 1868 federal treaty between the [[Crow Nation]] and the [[Federal government of the United States|U.S. Government]] is still in force even after [[Wyoming]] became a state in 1890. The treaty gave tribe members hunting rights on "unoccupied" lands. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-usa-court-hunter/us-supreme-court-sides-with-native-american-elk-hunter-idUSKCN1SQ1RN (Reuters)] [https://www.scotusblog.com/case-files/cases/herrera-v-wyoming/ (SCOTUS Blog)]
*[[Tax returns of Donald Trump]] 
**Judge [[Amit Mehta]] of the [[United States District Court for the District of Columbia]] rules that accounting firm [[Mazars]] must comply with a subpoena issued by the [[United States House Committee on Oversight and Reform]] to turn over U.S. President [[Donald Trump]]'s financial records. [https://www.nytimes.com/2019/05/20/us/politics/trump-financial-records.html (''The New York Times'')]

;Politics and elections
*[[Ukrainian presidential inauguration]]
**Former comedian and [[reality television]] actor [[Volodymyr Zelensky]] is sworn in as the 6th [[President of Ukraine]] by the [[Verkhovna Rada]]. Zelensky announces the  dissolution of parliament and calls a snap [[2019 Ukrainian parliamentary election|parliamentary election]]. [https://www.dw.com/cda/en/ukraine-president-zelenskiy-disbands-parliament-on-inauguration-day/a-48800069 (Deutsche Welle)]
**Ukrainian Prime Minister [[Volodymyr Groysman]] announces he will  resign Wednesday in response to the new president's disbanding of parliament. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2019/05/ukraine-prime-minister-resigns-protest-190520155817398.html (Al Jazeera)]
*[[Ibiza affair]]
**All ministers from the far-right [[Freedom Party of Austria]], who make up close to half of [[First Kurz government|Austria's cabinet]], are resigning in response to their party leader,   [[Heinz-Christian Strache]] being forced to resign as [[Vice-Chancellor of Austria|Vice-Chancellor]] after a video was published Friday showing Strache's participation in a compromising video. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-europe-48335316 (BBC News)]
*[[2019 Venezuelan presidential crisis]]
**[[President of Venezuela|Venezuelan President]] [[Nicolás Maduro]] proposes early elections for Venezuela's [[National Assembly (Venezuela)|National Assembly]]. Opposition leader and [[President of the National Assembly of Venezuela|National Assembly President]] [[Juan Guaidó]] has stated a rejection of the proposal. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-latin-america-48345335 (BBC News)]
*After several months of negotiations, President [[Félix Tshisekedi]] names [[Sylvestre Ilunga Ilukamba]] as the new [[Prime Minister of the Democratic Republic of the Congo]] in an agreement with former president [[Joseph Kabila]]. He had not appointed a prime minister since being elected in [[2018 Democratic Republic of the Congo general election|December 2018]]. [https://www.yahoo.com/news/dr-congo-political-heavyweight-moise-katumbi-returns-home-135221830.html (Yahoo! News)]

;Science and technology
*The [[2019 redefinition of SI base units|redefinition]] of the [[International System of Units|SI system]] of measurement [[Metrication|adopted]] by the majority of countries in the world takes effect. [https://www.bipm.org/en/measurement-units/ (BIPM)]
